executive_summary: Edinburgh and Austin sit at either end of a trading relationship worth $20.6bn a year, with no nonstop between them. Austin has grown its economy 36.4% in five years. Edinburgh is the most productive city in the United Kingdom outside London and handled a record 17m passengers in 2025, on a runway that already takes the A321XLR.

blocks.economic_context: Two economies growing faster than their national averages, with nothing direct between them. Austin's metropolitan output reached $268.4B after 36.4% growth in five years, the fastest of any United States metro. Edinburgh is now the most productive city in the United Kingdom outside London. Neither is a mature market being fought over.
blocks.trade: The commercial relationship is built and it flies through somebody else's hub. Texas and the United Kingdom traded $20.6bn in 2024, and British companies have put $9.8bn into Texas over the decade, more projects than any other country. Scotland has sent more of its exports to the United States than anywhere else every year since 2008.
blocks.corporate_links: The front cabin is already employed at both ends. Cirrus Logic is headquartered in Austin and employs around 350 people in Edinburgh, one company inside a semiconductor cluster of more than 60,000 in the Austin region. Amazon chose Edinburgh for its first development centre outside the United States. The corporate map reads the same in both cities.
blocks.tourism: The United States is Scotland's largest visitor market and its highest spending. Americans made 964,339 trips to Scotland in 2024 and spent £1,441m, over a third of all overseas spend. The seasonality helps: the Fringe issued 2,604,404 tickets in August, while Austin fills in March and October. Two festival cities with opposite peaks.
blocks.diaspora: Visiting friends and relatives is the ballast under a thin long-haul route, and Scotland has more of it than most. Upwards of 40m people worldwide consider themselves of Scottish descent, and 5.3m Americans claimed Scottish ancestry at the last census. This traffic books early, travels outside the peak and is far less fare-sensitive than leisure.
blocks.education: Student traffic fills the months either side of summer and repeats every year. 3,090 University of Edinburgh students were domiciled in the United States in 2024/25, its largest Western market. The University of Texas at Austin enrolled a record 55,000 students. The two already run a reciprocal exchange, so the flow is established rather than speculative.
blocks.passenger_profile: The market travels today, it simply travels the long way round. 229,000 United Kingdom residents visited Texas in 2024, split evenly between leisure and everything else. Austin's single United Kingdom nonstop carried 247,562 passengers last year and grew 21.7%. Everyone else connects, and KLM alone moved 76,254 through Amsterdam.
blocks.airport_overview: Edinburgh can take the aeroplane today. The airport handled a record 17m passengers in 2025 and serves 155 destinations across 37 airlines. Its 2560m runway already supports Boeing 787 and A321XLR transatlantic operations, so nothing on the ground has to change. Austin is investing to receive it, with a programme estimated at $5bn.
blocks.non_cannibalization: A nonstop from Edinburgh adds traffic to Scotland rather than moving it. Edinburgh already carries 55% of all Scottish air passengers, and a quarter of its domestic traffic runs to Heathrow, much of it connecting onward and carried by somebody else. Inbound passengers rose 40% between 2019 and 2025 while outbound fell 6%.
blocks.case_study: This has stopped being hypothetical. American Airlines returned to Edinburgh from Philadelphia in 2025, pointedly not from New York, and has chosen Edinburgh for the first international A321XLR route. JetBlue opened Boston the same month. United returns to Glasgow on a 166-seat narrowbody. Aer Lingus has used the same aircraft to open Nashville from Dublin.
